contents.name: Definition 2.2 — Empirical error or empirical risk
Footnote 2 — Measurability required for risk and empirical-error definitions
Equation (2.3) — Expected empirical error of a fixed hypothesis equals its risk
contents.reason: This fixed-hypothesis identity uses iid sampling and expectation linearity; ML-01 defines the risks but proves no sampling expectation theorem, so the finite-class learning page is the appropriate home.

contents.name: Definition 2.3 — PAC learning
contents.reason: PAC quantifiers, confidence and sample-complexity guarantees are outside ML-01's prediction/risk/ERM scope and are assigned to the finite-class PAC page.

contents.name: Example 2.4 — Learning axis-aligned rectangles
contents.reason: The geometric four-region argument is an example of a realizable PAC guarantee, not an example needed to define prediction risk or empirical minimization.

contents.name: Theorem 2.5 — Learning bound for finite H in the consistent case
contents.reason: The full iid finite-class realizable theorem and its bad-consistent-hypothesis proof belong to ML-02; ML-01 makes no generalization-bound claim.

contents.name: Example 2.6 — Conjunctions of Boolean literals
contents.reason: This source example applies the finite-class realizable sample bound and is outside the four ML-01 example themes.

contents.name: Corollary 2.10 — Fixed-hypothesis Hoeffding deviations
contents.reason: The concentration inequality depends on iid binary observations and is a prerequisite for the later finite-class learning guarantee, not a risk definition.

contents.name: Corollary 2.11 — Single-hypothesis generalization bound
contents.reason: The confidence bound for one fixed hypothesis is a concentration result; this pair does not assert finite-sample deviation guarantees.

contents.name: Example 2.12 — Tossing a biased coin
contents.reason: The coin calculation illustrates the single-hypothesis concentration bound and is better placed with the later finite-class PAC examples.

contents.name: Theorem 2.13 — Learning bound for finite H in the inconsistent case
contents.reason: The uniform finite-class deviation theorem and its Hoeffding/union-bound proof are assigned to ML-02, not this definition-and-algorithm page.

contents.name: Definition 2.14 — Agnostic PAC learning
contents.reason: The high-probability agnostic PAC guarantee and its sample-size quantifiers are not part of the ML-01 prediction-problem definition.

contents.name: Definition 2.16 — Pointwise classification noise
contents.reason: This pointwise binary-noise function is not needed for general Bayes-risk definitions or the four planned finite examples, and no later ML-01 claim uses it.
